title: Where confidence comes from, and how to question your inner critic

say: Where confidence comes from, and how to question your inner critic.
This is the video for module one of Confidence Building and Self-Belief.
Confidence is not feeling no fear. Psychologists call it self-efficacy: your belief that you can handle a particular task.
It is about a task, not your whole self. You can be sure of yourself cooking for fifty guests, and unsure about speaking at a PTA meeting.

panel.heading: Four sources of I can do this
items: Mastery: doing it yourself and succeeding
Watching someone like you succeed
Encouragement from people you trust
How you read your body and mood

say: The strongest source is mastery: doing the task yourself and succeeding, even in small steps. Like selling your first ten bottles of zobo and getting paid.

say: Most of us carry a harsh inner critic. You cannot switch it off, but you can question it.
For example, Amaka, a hairdresser in Owerri, gave a short report at her women's fellowship. Her voice shook and she lost her place once.

panel.heading: Amaka's thought record
items: Situation: a two-minute report at fellowship
Thought: I am useless at speaking
Feeling: shame, 80 out of 100
Evidence: figures correct, two women thanked her
Balanced thought, then shame drops to 35

say: Her automatic thought: everybody saw I was shaking. I am useless at speaking. That trap is called labelling.

panel.heading: Amaka's thought record

Thought: I am useless at speaking

Evidence: figures correct, two women thanked her

say: She names the feeling, shame, and rates it 80 out of 100.

panel.heading: Amaka's thought record

say: Now the facts. Her voice shook. But she gave all the figures correctly, two women thanked her, and the chairlady asked her to report again next month.

panel.heading: Amaka's thought record
items: Situation: a two-minute report at fellowship
Thought: I am useless at speaking
Feeling: shame, 80 out of 100
Evidence: figures correct, two women thanked her
Balanced thought, then shame drops to 35

say: Her balanced thought: I was nervous and lost my place once, and I still delivered a clear, correct report. Her shame drops to 35.
Do not swap I am useless for I am the best speaker in Nigeria. Your mind will reject it. Use and: I was nervous, and I did it.

panel.rule: A balanced thought is fair and believable, not falsely positive.

say: Many beliefs about ourselves were learned before we could question them. What happened is fixed.

panel.heading: What happened, or what I concluded?
right: I will never amount to much
I am not a business person

say: But the conclusion you drew can be tested now. For example, Halima left school after JSS3 because her family could not pay fees, and a teacher called her too slow.
Today she keeps accurate records for about 60 credit customers and learned a POS terminal in one week. Her updated belief: I missed school because of money, not ability.

say: Being humble is good. But hiding your skills is shrinking, and your customers and community lose what you could give.

panel.heading: Say what you did, without boasting

cards.d: It was nothing, anybody could do it.
Without me, this event would have collapsed.
Thank you. I organised the catering for 150 guests and it went well.

say: Arrogance goes the other way. It needs other people to be smaller.

panel.heading: Say what you did, without boasting

cards.d: It was nothing, anybody could do it.
Without me, this event would have collapsed.
Thank you. I organised the catering for 150 guests and it went well.

say: Healthy confidence states facts, says thank you, and puts nobody down.
When someone praises you, say thank you, full stop. For example, Funmi used to say, it was nothing. Now she says thank you, and asks her manager what she could do better next time.

panel.heading: Say what you did, without boasting

say: To remember. Confidence grows task by task, from small actions. Check your thoughts against facts. Test old beliefs with today's evidence. And accept praise with thank you.
This course is not therapy. If your inner voice says there is no point in living, do not handle it alone. Speak to a doctor or health worker as soon as you can. In an emergency in Nigeria, call 112.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Confidence is belief you can handle a task
Small tasks done yourself are the strongest source
Check thoughts against facts
Separate what happened from what you concluded
Thank you, full stop, then ask for feedback
